name: One Arm Joe
description: One Arm Joe (One-Armed Pete) is a one-card variant of Indian Poker. Each player receives one card face-down, holds it to their forehead so everyone else can see it but they cannot, then bets. Highest card at showdown wins the pot. A game of pure deduction and bluff.

content.text: One Arm Joe (One-Armed Pete) is a one-card variant of Indian Poker. Each player receives one card face-down, holds it to their forehead so everyone else can see it but they cannot, then bets. Highest card at showdown wins the pot. A game of pure deduction and bluff.

Indian Pokerâ€”cards held to the forehead so others see your card but you do notâ€”originated in America. The name has nothing to do with India; it refers to cards resembling a headdress. One Arm Joe and One-Armed Pete are regional names for the one-card variant.

Two to eight players. The one-card variant is the basic form: each player is dealt one card face down, picks it up without looking, and holds it against the forehead so all others can see its value. A round of betting follows; at showdown the highest card among those who did not fold wins the pot. The game is usually played with 2–8; skills involved are probability and reading other players' actions and bets.
Standard 52-card deck. Ace high; no suit ranking for ties.
Each player antes. Dealer deals one card face-down to each player. Players pick up their card without looking, hold it facing outward, and place it against their forehead so all others can see it.

items.text: Low Wins: Lowest card wins instead of highest. Otherwise identical.
High-Low Split: Best high card and best low card split the pot.
Match Pot: Stay/drop declaration; best card wins; others who stayed must match the pot.
Two-Card Indian: Deal two cards each; best hand wins. Less common; not much more strategic.
